name: Fedor Panov
identity: Fedor E. Panov, MD — Associate Professor of Neurosurgery & Director, Adult Epilepsy Surgery Program, Mount Sinai Health System / Icahn School of Medicine (New York, NY).
bio: Board-certified functional/epilepsy neurosurgeon whose practice centers on the surgical treatment of drug-resistant epilepsy and movement disorders. Case mix is dominated by minimally invasive epilepsy work — stereo-EEG (SEEG) mapping, laser ablation (LITT), responsive neurostimulation (RNS), and DBS/focused ultrasound — consistent with claims showing very high SEEG (91) and epilepsy craniotomy (122) volume plus a smaller but real LITT footprint (8). He directs Mount Sinai's adult epilepsy surgery program and has published 50+ manuscripts in epilepsy/neuromodulation.
training: MD, Sidney Kimmel/Jefferson Medical College (Thomas Jefferson University), Philadelphia · Neurosurgery residency, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai · Fellowships: Epilepsy Neurosurgery, UCSF (Edward Chang) and Movement Disorders Neurosurgery, UCSF (Philip Starr / Paul Larson) · Pedigree note: UCSF Chang/Starr functional-neurosurgery lineage — a top-tier epilepsy/functional pedigree.

litt_platform: Visualase (Medtronic) — competitor equipment per claims cohort.
litt_exposure: Hands-on LITT operator. Claims show litt_perf = 8 ablations, embedded in a high-volume SEEG-driven epilepsy program (seeg 91, epi_cranio 122) that he directs, so LITT is used as the ablation arm after SEEG localization (mesial temporal, insular, hypothalamic hamartoma, SEEG-guided focus ablation are program indications). No LITT-specific paper was verified under his direct authorship, so evidence is claims + program role rather than a citable LITT publication.
wheelhouse: SEEG-first functional/epilepsy neurosurgeon — minimally invasive epilepsy surgery with laser ablation + neuromodulation (RNS/DBS).
kol_note: Directs the Adult Epilepsy Surgery Program at Mount Sinai and runs its neurosurgery pre-residency fellowship; 50+ publications across epilepsy neuromodulation/SEEG (PNAS, Neurosurgery, Ann Clin Transl Neurol, J Neurosurg Pediatr). Regional academic KOL in functional/epilepsy neurosurgery, though not a published LITT-technique thought leader specifically.
